title: Three Days and One Short Pencil
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：map　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 map 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the traveller ① drew the map that no porter in the pass would have recorded, and he said the drawing was the whole of the day. The ② map, meaning the chart itself and not the pencil, ran three days and stayed unrecorded in the book; a map, he said, is the only thing in a pass that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ map in that pass had the same short pencil beside it, and the ④ map at the far ledge, meaning the trail they kept for the children to trace and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A map, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the traveller said the recording is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the map was the whole of the matter, meaning the direction and not the chart. The ⑥ map, meaning the direction and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; map, he said, is either something you draw or the only word that means both a chart and a direction. He said the direction is the part they remember.

By 1986 the ⑦ map had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short pencil. The ⑧ map of the whole thing, the traveller wrote in July, was one pass and three days of recording; map, he said, is either the trail at the far ledge or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ map I remember is the chart recorded in the journal, which closed in 1988 and is still recorded as the quietest in the pass. A ⑩ map, my mother said in 1990, is the only chart that improves by being recorded; every map, she said, is a direction that has agreed to look like a chart. She said the direction was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 地图；图（指山口里每一张旁边的那一张）
B. n. 地图；图（指那张地图本身，与铅笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：draw the map 绘制这张地图
D. n. 地图；图（指留给孩子们描的那一条那一张）
E. n. 行路之事（抽象总称，指一处山口的地图之事）
F. n. 地图；图（指行记里写到、被记载的的那一张）
G. n. 方向、路程（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 路程（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: draw the map 意为“绘制这张地图”，1981 年那位旅人把山口里没有一位挑夫肯记载的一张地图做了一遍。
map 意为“地图；图”，指那张地图本身而不是铅笔，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被记载。
map 意为“地图；图”，指山口里每一张旁边的那一张，每一张旁边都有同一支短短的铅笔。
map 意为“地图；图”，指最远那处崖台留给孩子们描的那一条那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
map 意为“方向、路程”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个方向就是那件事的全部。
map 意为“路程”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那张地图，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
map 意为“地图；图”，指行记里写到、被记载的的那一张，到 1986 年这一张成了行记里的一行。
map 意为“行路之事”，旅人七月写道，整件事的地图之事是一处山口和三个日子的记载。
map 意为“地图；图”，我记得的是行记里记载过的那一张，1988 年画完了，至今仍被说成山口里最安静的一张。
map 为抽象总称，母亲 1990 年说，地图是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的地图。
